title: Platform Ops Fastpitch — Sprint Notes (WIP)
content:
Purpose / context:
- Create a compact "fastpitch" deck and companion micro-battlecard for field engineers and platform sellers.
- Target: platform engineering leads and SREs evaluating inference for production (pilot -> dedicated).
- Constraint: 6 slides + 1 one-pager battlecard (30s pitch, technical checklist, fallback plan). Time box: 2-week sprint for a field-ready draft.

Audience and outcomes:
- Primary: Platform engineers (integration architects), SEs running pilot conversations.
- Secondary: AE/SDR for qualification.
- Outcome: enable SE to run a 10–15 minute pilot scoping call and leave a 1-pager that maps to next steps: pilot scope, KPIs, trial timeline.

Slide outline (rough):
1) Hook (30s): "Predictable inference economics across your fleet" — 1 headline, 1 stat (median p95 tokens/latency from our bench), 1 customer example (anonymized). Speaker note: lead with SLA+cost tradeoffs rather than model accuracy.
2) Where Redwood sits in stack: small diagram (app -> orchestration -> Redwood runtime -> GPUs/private infra). Callouts: routing policies, KV caching, quantization profiles. Speaker note: keep high level; avoid deep runtime jargon.
3) Pilot blueprint (what we ship in 2 weeks): reserved pool, probe traffic, canonical prompt set, latency SLO target, success metric (cost per 1k tokens + 95th latency).
4) Compatibility and integration checklist (battle-ready): network/firewall, auth (API key vs mTLS), model artifact size, preferred CUDA/Driver matrix, data egress constraints. Add quick T-shoot tips.
5) Fallback and reliability story: model variants, regional fallback, autoscaling policy for bursts. Show an example flow: p95 spike -> scale policy -> if unavailable -> fallback model degrade gracefully.
6) Pricing/commit framing + next steps: pilot cost estimate template + a 4-step handoff to Solutions Eng.

One-pager micro-battlecard (front pocket):
- 30s opener: "You want predictable latency at scale with transparent unit economics — Redwood maps to both via routing + caching + reserved capacity."
- Key buyer signals: high qps LLM calls, regulatory constraints, multiregion traffic, ops team managing infra.
- Tech qual checklist (rapid):
  * Expected RPS / peak tokens per sec? -> number
  * Max sequence length typical? -> number
  * Model family (LlamaX / Mistral / GPT-style?) -> yes/no
  * Can you expose endpoint to our VPC peering or do we deploy private? -> choose
  * Key compliance requirement? (SOC2, HIPAA)
- Quick objection scripts:
  * "We host models internally; why Redwood?" -> "We reduce ops cost by 40–60% via batching, KV caching, and precompiled kernels; plus fallbacks and SLA that your infra needs to own."
  * "Latency concerns for interactive product" -> "We can reserve capacity and tune batch windows; show p95 numbers from similar pilot (example included)."
  * "Proprietary data safety" -> "Private plane + KMS, audit logs, optional on-prem box for air-gapped."

Operational hooks / demo checklist (for SE):
- Before call: prepare pilot cost worksheet (sheet template link in linked_artifacts).
- During call: collect answers to Tech qual checklist and capture model artifact size + sample prompt set.
- After call: open pilot ticket with Solutions Eng (JIRA-OPS-4123 template), drop onboarding link to customer (one-liner).

Metrics to capture in pilot (so we can quantify wins):
- Baseline: customer p95 latency and cost/token with current setup
- Pilot: median p95 latency, tokens/unit cost, cache hit ratio, CPU/GPU utilization, tail latency during peak.
- Goal: show >=20% cost reduction or <=50ms p95 improvement vs baseline (one of these).

Unresolved questions / open items (notes to self):
- Need realistic example numbers for the deck (benchmarks spanning 512 vs 2048 token contexts). Action: ask Applied ML for a short table (Rohit).
- Add a short slide for "what we need from you" (customer-side) with exact network rules and sample prompt set.
- Legal/Procurement ask: a minimal pilot agreement template for customers in EU (privacy wording). Who owns? Samira to prod.

Slide content drafts (bullets / speaker notes) — rough copy:
Slide 1 headline: "Predictable inference economics for production LLMs"
- Speaker: "Many teams hit unpredictable bills or tail latency surprises. We bring unit economics + SLOs together so you can ship while controlling cost."
- Stat line: "Pilot customers see 25–45% unit cost reduction after caching + batching." (PLACEHOLDER)

Slide 2: "Where Redwood sits"
- bullets: "Unified API, routing policies, GPU-optimized runtime, private deployment options."
- Speaker: emphasize "same API for hosted/dedicated/private"

Slide 3: "Pilot blueprint (2 weeks)"
- bullets: "reserve pool 16 vGPU equivalent; 3 day probe traffic; canonical prompts; success gates: p95 <= target; cost delta documented."

Slide 4: "Integration checklist (5 minute qual)"
- bullets: "Network (VPC peering or IP allowlist), Auth (API key/mTLS), Model artifact (weights + config), Compliance ask"

Slide 5: "Fallbacks & reliability"
- bullets: "model variants, region fallback, autoscale policy, graceful degrade"

Slide 6: "Estimate + next steps"
- bullets: "pilot cost estimate, roll-to-dedicated path, AE > SE > Solutions Eng handoff"

Appendix ideas (optional slides):
- short benchmark table (512/1024/2048 token p50/p95),
- quick primer on quantization profiles and their tradeoffs,
- customer case snippet (sanitized).

Action items (two-week sprint):
- [ ] Pull bench numbers from Applied ML (Rohit) — due 2025-11-07
- [ ] Draft minimal pilot agreement (Samira) — due 2025-11-10
- [ ] Build slide deck skeleton and 1-pager battlecard (Maya) — due 2025-11-14
- [ ] Internal review with Solutions Eng and SRE (Diego) — schedule by 2025-11-12

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the deck snappy — SEs need a 6-slide artifact they can present in 6 minutes.
- Avoid heavy developer docs in the deck; link to more detailed runbook in Confluence.
- We should create a one-click pilot cost estimator (sheet) later — not this sprint.

References and scraps:
- Competitor angle: highlight our unified runtime + private option vs pure open-source stacks that require heavy ops.
- Scratch slide: fallback flow diagram ascii:
  REQUEST -> ROUTER (policy: latency/cost) -> RUNTIME -> if overload -> FALLBACK MODEL -> DEGRADE RESPONSE (structured)

End of notes — wip.
